column1: # UTF-8 tab-separated: kind, language, key, value
# Sentence language: a Korean sentence reads embedded foreign material in Korean;
# Hangul written against another script (meeting은, 3시에) is Korean grammar.
# One eojeol holds a word with its particles and endings: it counts as two words
# against another script (update 안내 update stays Korean).
# Particle agreement after a spoken reading: consonant|vowel[|rieul] forms.
# Only obligatory allomorphs; optional copula contractions (이며/며) keep their text.
# 로/으로 keeps 로 after a ㄹ final consonant.
# Obligatory noun-particle pairs; exact spans only, never arbitrary word prefixes.
# See docs/particle-resources.md for the policy, sources and editing procedure.
# Both written forms also close numeric quantities and signal Korean context.
# 하루에 다섯 번뿐이다: 뿐 is a particle (2026-10-07).
